answer: A split needs an owned completion or partial-release rule because, without a known part count, completion is not decidable: the aggregate group stays incomplete indefinitely rather than completing silently (Spring Integration sets SEQUENCE_SIZE to zero for an unknown-size iterator and leaves the group incomplete). Left alone, that open group holds tracking state and leaks orphaned work, so someone must own when to stop waiting. A custom ReleaseStrategy or send-partial-result-on-expiry provides that rule: it releases a partial result or forces closure, defines partial-result disposition and compensation ownership, and bounds fan-out. Critically, release or expiry closure is only a forced/partial closure, not evidence of successful completion; the same page's decision rule therefore requires either a known total count or an explicit release rule or expiry before splitting, and says a split with no completion marker leaks orphaned work and needs an owner.
